questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My major is Japanese studies, so exchanging to Japan seemed obvious.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had received handouts prior to my arrival, so it was very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Various introductions. Like the dorm, or the campus.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Osaka University offers student accommodations off campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I stayed at Global Village, which is a little far from Suita Campus if you walk (especially during summer).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You "pick" courses 3 times in total, which I think is superfluous, but the process is easy enough.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The OUSSEP office was reachable via email, and you could ask staff at the dorm for help, if needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to take all my classes except for one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are some deadlines they want you to honor, but if you suddenly find out you want a different class, or drop a class, they will usually help you out, from what I heard from friends.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some have a high work-load, others a very light one. The level itself is not that high, because you're taking 7+ courses. This is regarding the OUSSEP exchange courses. I can't speak for the regular classes at OU which I assume are on a higher level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More lecture-style classes at OU. UCPH has more seminar-style classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Health Service and Medical Care in Japan 
Osaka in Modern Japanese Literature
Japan: Society and Ideology
Introduction to Japanese Law
Digital Culture: Literature and Art, Ethics and Aesthetics
Critical Thinking in a Global Context: Navigating the Challenges Ahead
Cultural Psychological Experiment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Osaka in Modern Literate is really interesting and has an amazing teacher. Highly recommend.
Health Service and Medical Care in Japan is good if you want a laid back course.

questions.answer: The move-in date the dorm wants you to arrive by is not mandatory what-so-ever. They advise the last month of march, but unless you REALLY want to go as soon as possible, I'd wait till the 1st of April, as they will charge you a full month of rent and rental fees for those 1-7 days.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: More or less as I expected. Food is cheap, except fruit.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Literally hundreds of clubs and circles to join. Something for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I'm sure anything is fine, but I joined the English Conversation club (takakomi) to socialize with Japanese people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
It's Japan, I'm sure you can think of something, but I recommend going to Kyoto. Endless amounts of temples and cool places to see.
Koyasan in Wakayama is also really cool, and maybe my favorite cultural site.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was my second exchange in Japan, so I acclimated fairly easily.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs/circles.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The bureaucracy is tiresome, but you can sort of everything the first week and last week of your stay, so it's not too bad.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The safety. The kindness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Keep the deadlines that OU ask of you. You'll be less stressed.
- Get a Japanese speaking person to go with you to the City Hall, as it will speed up the process, and you avoid mishaps (though you'll be fine even without one).
- At the immigration booth at the airport, be sure to ask about your Certificate of Eligibility (you will have received one from OU ELECTRONICALLY). They will ask for the physical original, but you won't receive it. Be adamant about it, because this is where you get your residence card.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I covered it all.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to use my Japanese, and making friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The summer. Spring is awesome, but the summer is rough.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to Karaoke! Other than the traditional cultural stuff, karaoke was my favorite activity in Japan.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
